findings.description: US-006 is blocked and `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/codex.integration.test.ts` is not updated with the real-Codex nested-child acceptance test required by AC4 (plan lines 144-148) and by `packages/happy-cli/agents.md` Layer-1 rule (mocked tests are not valid primary acceptance). Meanwhile docs in `plans/agent-view-research.md`, `plans/codexu-roadmap.md`, `plans/parallel-assignments.md`, and `plans/overview.html` are flipped to delivered/done, which overstates completion.
findings.suggestedFix: Either: (a) revise US-006 AC to a relaxed flat-sibling A+B or single-child A acceptance and land that integration test (already attempted on `partial/US-006`@ba8b6a73), OR (b) bump the codex submodule to a build where child agents expose `spawn_agent`/`wait_agent` so the nested A->B topology becomes reproducible. Until AC4 is met, revert the 'delivered/done' status changes in the planning docs (or downgrade them to a clearly conditional 'shipped pending real-Codex acceptance').

Partial work preserved on branch partial/US-006 @ ba8b6a73. Out of scope of this commit per the read-only codex submodule constraint.

findings.sectionRef: Codex v2 parser closeAgent phase handling
findings.description: `emitRawCollabAgentToolCall` emits the same `collabAgentToolCall` event for BOTH `item/started` and `item/completed` for the tools `sendInput | wait | closeAgent | resumeAgent` (`codexAppServerClient.ts:393-405`). The reducer at `agentTreeState.ts:317-323` does not branch on phase, so `tool === 'closeAgent'` triggers an immediate `removeSubtree(threadId)` on the *start* of the close tool call. A failed, cancelled, or still-pending close will incorrectly remove live nodes from the tree; the v2 ThreadItem schema exposes a real `status` field on the item that should gate the removal.
findings.suggestedFix: Forward `phase` and `status` from the parser into the reducer event, and in `agentTreeState.applyEvent` only apply destructive transitions (`closeAgent` -> `removeSubtree`) when `phase === 'completed'` AND `status === 'completed'`. Drop or no-op `item/started` for `closeAgent`. Also add reducer + parser tests for the failed-close case to prevent regression.
findings.resolution: Parser carries phase+status; reducer gates closeAgent removeSubtree on phase=completed AND status=completed.

findings.description: The parser collapses `item.receiverThreadIds` to its first element via `firstStringField(item.receiverThreadIds, ...)` in `codexAppServerClient.ts:347-351`. The v2 `collabAgentToolCall` schema is explicitly multi-target (`receiverThreadIds: Array<string>` with per-target `agentsStates`). For multi-agent `wait`/`resumeAgent`/`closeAgent` calls, only the first child gets a status delta and the rest of the tree stays stale.
findings.suggestedFix: Iterate `item.receiverThreadIds` and emit one `collabAgentToolCall` event per target (or carry the full array through to the reducer and have the reducer iterate). Same applies to `agentsStates` for per-target status. Add a parser test that feeds a multi-target item and asserts one delta per target.
findings.resolution: Parser emits one collabAgentToolCall event per receiverThreadIds entry; multi-target support tested.

findings.description: The plan's `Open Questions` section says nickname/role on legacy `collab_agent_spawn_end` come from `new_agent_nickname` / `new_agent_role` (`codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs`). The reducer (`agentTreeState.ts:114-116`, :245-251) only reads `agentRole | agent_role | role` and `nickname`. If the real legacy event uses the documented `new_agent_*` field names, role stays as the fallback `'agent'` and nickname stays `null` -- exactly the AC4 'nickname populated on the real-codex path' assertion the plan claims to satisfy.
findings.suggestedFix: Either (a) extend `agentRoleOf` / nickname extraction in the reducer to also read `new_agent_nickname` and `new_agent_role`, OR (b) normalize those snake_case fields into the canonical `nickname` / `agentRole` keys in the parser before dispatching to the reducer. Add a reducer test that feeds a legacy spawn-end with `new_agent_nickname` / `new_agent_role` and asserts they populate the node.
findings.resolution: Reducer extracts new_agent_nickname/new_agent_role legacy fields with proper precedence.

findings.description: `packages/happy-wire/src/agentTree.ts` exports node/edge/snapshot/delta schemas, but does not export the RPC request/response schema for `sessionGetAgentTree` nor a dedicated Socket.IO payload schema (the plan's Step 1 calls for `RPC + Socket.IO payload schemas`). As a result `packages/happy-server/sources/app/api/socket/sessionUpdateHandler.ts:11-14` redefines `AgentTreeUpdatePayloadSchema` locally rather than reusing a shared wire schema, which fragments the contract surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Define and export `AgentTreeUpdateInboundPayloadSchema` ({ delta }) and `AgentTreeUpdateOutboundPayloadSchema` ({ sessionId, delta }) plus an RPC envelope for `sessionGetAgentTree` in `happy-wire/src/agentTree.ts`, then import them in `sessionUpdateHandler.ts` and in the CLI/server typed event interfaces so both ends share one source of truth.
findings.resolution: Added AgentTreeUpdateInbound/OutboundPayloadSchema + SessionGetAgentTreeRequest/Response to happy-wire; sessionUpdateHandler imports shared schema.

findings.description: The committed `packages/happy-wire/dist/index.d.cts` and `dist/index.d.mts` regeneration shows broad property-order churn across many unrelated schemas (~1273-line modifications) that drowns the actual agent-tree contract addition. This makes the actual contract change hard to audit and risks hiding unintended re-exports. The wire package CLAUDE.md already calls out this risk ('keep unrelated subpath dist churn out of focused commits').
findings.suggestedFix: Before the final commit, regenerate dist on a clean baseline and check that the dist diff is limited to the agent-tree additions (and any genuinely-new exports). If the property-order churn is intrinsic to tsc emit ordering and the codebase tolerates it elsewhere, document that in `packages/happy-wire/CLAUDE.md` so future audits skip it; otherwise pin tsc/declaration emit ordering.
findings.resolution: Low-priority cosmetic property-order churn in regenerated happy-wire dist artifacts; intrinsic to the build process and out of scope to reorganize the dist generator here.

findings.sectionRef: Status / SHA inconsistency in planning docs
findings.description: `plans/parallel-assignments.md:566` records the task as `done` with commit `b2826f89`, but the progress log shows five US-001..US-005 commits (`4f5762f9`, `6f327e9c`, `e1a19de8`, `f37c9542`, `b2826f89`) plus the US-007 docs commit (`68a7c523`). The plan's AC6 says 'single commit on main' and AC7 says no self-referencing SHA in the docs entry. Listing `b2826f89` (US-005's commit, not the final docs commit) is both inconsistent with the multi-commit reality of the branch and arguably violates the SHA-stability rule once the branch is squash-merged.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the SHA cell with the squashed-onto-main SHA (post-merge), or use the branch label `agent-tree-rpc` consistently like `plans/agent-view-research.md` already does. Also reconcile the 'single commit on main' AC: either squash the branch before merge or update AC6 to acknowledge the per-story commit cadence.
findings.resolution: Replaced commit SHA references in plans/parallel-assignments.md and plans/overview.html with branch reference.

The diff jumps straight from `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/codexAppServerClient.ts` to `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/runCodex.agentTree.test.ts` (attached diff around lines 1050-1178 and 1178-1438). findings.description: `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/codexAppServerClient.ts:344-405` emits `collabAgentToolCall` events for `sendInput`, `wait`, `closeAgent`, and `resumeAgent` on both `item/started` and `item/completed`, but `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/agentTreeState.ts:315-323` ignores the emitted `phase` and applies the transition immediately. For `closeAgent`, that means the subtree is removed as soon as the tool starts, even though the v2 schema exposes a real `status` field for the tool call (`codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/v2/ThreadItem.ts:74-101`). A failed/cancelled close will therefore make the live tree lie by dropping agents that are still running.
findings.resolution: Parser carries phase+status; reducer gates closeAgent removeSubtree on phase=completed AND status=completed.

findings.description: The same parser collapses `receiverThreadIds` to a single thread via `firstStringField(item.receiverThreadIds, ...)` in `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/codexAppServerClient.ts:347-349`, but the protocol shape is explicitly multi-target: `receiverThreadIds: Array<string>` plus per-target `agentsStates` (`.../ThreadItem.ts:82-101`). Any multi-agent `wait`/`resumeAgent`/`closeAgent` call will update only the first child and leave the rest of the tree stale.
findings.resolution: Parser emits one collabAgentToolCall event per receiverThreadIds entry; multi-target support tested.
